items.title: Pay "processing fee" to release claimed refund
items.quote: überweisen Sie bitte die einmalige Bearbeitungsgebühr von 49,90 € bis zum 27.11.2026 auf das Konto IBAN CY17 0020 0128 0000 0012 0052 7600.
items.computation: The letter prints an explicit calendar date, 27.11.2026, as the deadline for the payment. 27.11.2026 is a Friday, not a weekend or public holiday, so no adjustment under § 193 BGB is needed. However, this payment is to an account in Cyprus for an unverifiable private 'refund office', not a legitimate German authority or known company, so the whole demand is almost certainly fraudulent (advance-fee / upfront-fee scam) and should not be paid.

warnings: This letter matches the classic advance-fee ('Vorkasse') fraud pattern: a large, unexpected refund (612,00 €) is promised, but only released after the recipient first pays a smaller upfront 'processing fee' (49,90 €) — in such scams the large sum is never actually paid out.

The fee must be sent to a Cyprus IBAN (CY17 0020 0128 0000 0012 0052 7600), and the sender's address is in Nikosia, Zypern; no genuine German energy-cost refund scheme operates this way or uses a foreign account for a German consumer.

'Verbraucher-Rückerstattungsstelle Energie' is not a known, registered German authority or regulator; the name is designed to sound official but there is no such public body responsible for energy-cost refunds.
The letter uses a pressure tactic ('Verstreicht die Frist, verfällt Ihr Anspruch endgültig.') to rush the recipient into paying quickly without verification, which is typical of scam mail.
Recommendation: do not transfer any money to this account, do not reply with personal or bank details, and report the letter to the Verbraucherzentrale and/or local police as suspected fraud.
